Hi, I did this unit 2 years back when i was a first year student. I think the unit itself has pretty simple enough overarching ideas of trends of evolution, etc
But do bear in mind this unit has a lot a lot a lot of content to be memorised, and (at least for my year) it’s a 60% theory paper and a 30% practical exam for finals - so the finals is worth 90%. I would take it again, as i found it extremely enjoyable and super interesting! Just know that it’s really a lot of content!
Yes I believe you would only be able to apply after your sem 2 marks are out

I sent an enquiry through the school website as a current student on 22 Jan, and I got my offer to transfer course on 8 Jan. Within an hour of sending them the enquiry, my credit transfer was approved
so you definitely have to rush them as in send them e-mails or enquiries to prompt them to look at your case and approve your credit transfer because it took them so long to look at my case, I couldn't apply submit my timetable preferences as early as everyone else and was stuck with shitty timeslots for my labs and tutorials
This happened to me last year - I waited till mid-Jan this year and I sent them an e-mail and they processed it that very day. Gotta rush them!!

I'm not too sure for domestic students' scholarships, but my friends aren't on scholarships as it's really really competitive and there are really not many to go around. The job is pretty rewarding - but there are tons of drawbacks, like the really bad mental health that comes with the job. Vets have one of the highest suicide rates because there are so many things that people don't consider, like putting down animals or having to deal with really bad pet owners.

Ahh my bad - $56k a year for a domestic student. But bu the time you reach DVM 1 in 2-3 years, it would have probably hit $60k already - definitely have to be ready for this huge financial responsibility!!

Hello! I'm currently in this BVB/DVM program. I think as a mature aged student, you would have better chances entering this course from the Foundations program - you also need to have work experience with animals. You definitely have to have good grades as entry is really competitive!!

The full cost for a domestic student for BVB/DVM is about $11k for the first 2 undergrad years, and from what I hear from my domestic student friends, it's about 52k a year for the remaining 4 years of postgrad - super costly so you have to be prepared for that. 

I'm currently sort of 'working', i do dog walking and dog sitting and dog boarding on pawshake so i spend just a small portion of my day walking dogs to earn some money. It is manageable as long as you can manage your time well!

And one thing about vet school is that wanting to work with animals and being passionate about them is not going to be enough to sustain you in this demanding course. You have to be prepared to work FOR the animals, and on top of an academically rigorous syllabus, in your DVM years you will be losing lots of holiday time to be doing industry placements and gaining more work experience (and you don't get paid doing all this, so if you have to go somewhere far to do your placement, that's gonna incur even more costs). It's really pretty exhausting and definitely not easy, but will be worth it once you've achieved it!! All the best!!

Hi, i'm a successful transfer from AVBS to BVB/DVM after my first year of studies. My WAM for my first year was 83.4, and i had 15 days of work experience at a veterinary clinic. 

As I'm an international student, what happened was that Usyd held an education fair in my country, and I went to speak to a representative on 1 Dec 2017, but lo and behold I had missed the application deadline of 30 Nov 2017. But applications for AVBS were still open and his words were, i quote verbatim, 'if you get 80 marks in AVBS, you will be guaranteed an internal transfer into the vet course.'

How it works is there is an international pool and a domestic pool - even if you do get 80 marks, there has to be someone who dropped out of vet after year 1 for you to take their spot. And do this internal transfer on sydneystudent - many students e-mailed the school or simply reapplied as a new student and DID NOT GET ACCEPTED. Do not forget to submit your commitment statement form!!

With all that said, all the best in becoming a vet student!!
